messages:
emma: FYI customer INC-4021 seeing repeated 401s + huge latency. They are pinned to eu-west-1 but responses show X-Steer-Region: us-east-1. Happened after yesterday's L7 rule push. Anyone able to look?
liam: can you paste a raw response (headers + resp time) and a request id? are they on Dedicated or Hosted?
emma: hosted. req_id=abc123def ts=2026-03-11T14:18:02Z. curl example and response below:
```
curl -v 'https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?region=eu-west-1' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
> GET /v1/generate?region=eu-west-1 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< X-Steer-Region: us-east-1
< X-Edge-Proxy: edge-a-3
< X-Request-Id: abc123def
< Content-Type: application/json
timings: dns 10ms connect 20ms ssl 30ms ttfb 1100ms total 1250ms
```
Also saw intermittent 401s earlier, billing spike reported by customer around same window.
michelle: escalated oncall already. Noted the request shows edge-a-3 which is a us-east pod. If the tenant is pinned to eu-west we shouldn't be steering them.
raj: I'm looking at the L7 config diff from yesterday: someone added a fallback policy that sets `x-steer-region` based on cluster capacity. The code path lives in envoy route config -> `regional_steering_filter`. It rewrites headers with `set_header x-steer-region %SELECTED_REGION%`. That might be overwriting the tenant pin header.
liam: not good. We intended fallback only for unpinned traffic. Could be a header precedence bug: new filter runs after tenant-pin filter.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Completed rollout `l7-regional-steer v1.4.2` to cluster edge-a (2026-03-11T13:55Z). Canary 10% -> 100%.
emma: customer timeline matches that rollout time.
raj: quick check: `kubectl -n edge get pod edge-a-3 -o yaml | grep -A3 regional_steer` shows filter order: regional_steer after header_pin. BUT the filter's implementation uses `replace_header` not `append_if_missing`. So even pinned headers are replaced when fallback triggers.
liam: ok that explains region flip. Next steps: 1) hotfix to change to `append_if_missing` or check pin flag, 2) revert rollout for edge-a until fix, 3) contact customer and ask them to retry.
michelle: I'm on the customer call now, they need ETA. Can we rollback now?
raj: initiating rollback to v1.4.1 on edge-a now. Command: `kubectl -n edge set image deploy/edge-proxy edge-proxy=ghcr.io/redwood/edge-proxy:v1.4.1` (will patch).
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started deployment rollback `l7-regional-steer -> v1.4.1` (2026-03-11T14:20Z). Health checks: in progress.
raj: rollback complete on edge-a. Verifying headers...
liam: re-run the curl that showed wrong header?
emma: re-ran for the same req_id window, new resp:
```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< X-Steer-Region: eu-west-1
< X-Edge-Proxy: edge-a-1
< X-Request-Id: abc123def-2
timings: dns 11ms connect 22ms ssl 31ms ttfb 120ms total 150ms
```
michelle: customer confirmed latency returned to normal and no more 401s. They saw billing spike disappeared after rollback.
liam: good. We'll push a proper fix in the next patch: change filter to respect `x-tenant-pin` header and use `append_if_missing`. Also add an e2e regression test that simulates pinned tenant traffic under fallback conditions.
raj: filing follow-up PR and will include config lint rule to fail if `replace_header` used in regional steering.
emma: thanks team. I'll update INC-4021 and close after customer confirms for 24h.
support-oncall: noted. Adding postmortem tag `pm-2026-03-11-regional-steer` and scheduling 30min blameless review tomorrow. :calendar:
